title: About Me
text:
I am currently a Data Scientist at Capture Higher Ed, based in Las Cruces, NM. I hold a B.S. in Biology with a minor in Applied Mathematics (2009) and an MS in Applied Statistics (2011), both from New Mexico State University.
After graduating, I worked for six years as a Data Analyst at HID Global’s Biometric Center of Excellence in Albuquerque, NM. In 2019, I joined the Data Sciences organization at Sandia National Laboratories as a Data Scientist. In 2022, I brought my experience to Capture Higher Ed, where I help develop predictive models for higher education enrollment. This role blends machine learning, MLOps, data engineering, and software development.
My professional interests include:

R programming and package development
Creating impactful data visualizations
User-centered design in code development.

In my free time, I enjoy gardening, cooking, and—despite my best efforts—occasionally killing houseplants.

title: Curriculum Vitae
text:
Professional Experience
Data Scientist, Capture Higher Ed, Louisville, KY, 08/2022–Present
Designed, implemented, and maintained internal- and partner-facing predictive models in R, Python, and SQL on AWS for a higher education enrollment management and marketing firm. Adapted predictions to institutions of differing size and geography through feature engineering and external data sources including census and school performance data. Enabled Customer Success and education advisors to apply model output to client enrollment strategy, and partnered with 9-12 client institutions to define how each counts enrollment, reconciling those definitions to a common internal standard so predictions stayed comparable across schools.

Assumed sole ownership of the enrollment prediction framework and codebase after its original author departed, extending it to become the company’s highest-rated product at 59 NPS across 80 users, with MAPE narrowing from 10% six months out to 1% by May.
Scoped 2 LLM-powered products with senior leadership, Product, Engineering, and Infrastructure, translating product requirements into technical approach and delivering both to general availability within a 6-month deadline, with an evaluation framework combining human graders, LLM-as-judge calibrated against human scores, and golden-dataset automated scoring.
Found that students visiting campus before applying enroll at near-certainty, redirecting client recruitment spend away from students already converting toward segments where outreach changes the outcome.
Engineered R Shiny application automating model validation across the data science team’s full book of 15-20 higher education clients, defining absolute, percent, and raw error measures across 15 prediction points and 5 models, replacing 3 manual checkpoints and surfacing seasonal patterns through exploratory analysis that improved subsequent predictions.
Consolidated scattered R scripts into main package infrastructure as a reusable analytical system, eliminating a single-person bottleneck so all 4 team members could generate client onboarding reports and reducing generation time from 2 days to 4 hours.
Recognized company-wide by peer vote for first-year impact, selected from 21 candidates across two hiring years (Rookie of the Year, 2023).
Assumed ownership of containerized development environment supporting the 4-person data science team’s production model deployment, implementing ARM architecture support to enable migration to faster machines and maintaining annual security updates for R/Python libraries and federal data sources.

Data Scientist, Sandia National Laboratories, Albuquerque, NM, 07/2018–08/2022
Built and deployed interactive applications for 2 predictive models and 4 data visualizations supporting safety, security, and employee retention at a federally funded national security laboratory. Delivered analysis to leadership on the performance of the $177.7 million Laboratory Directed Research & Development (LDRD) program. Streamlined access and data quality for 83 enterprise data sets using SQL and data virtualization (Denodo, Tibco) to join sources across systems into unified data streams, and established research software practices by documenting CI/CD pipelines in Docker and GitLab. Presented on visualization tooling and safety model deployment at the National Laboratories IT Summit (2019).

Won competitive CIO funding (1 of 3 from ~20 proposals) to co-develop the enterprise data visualization style guide for research figures and business dashboards, achieving 28% adoption across a 14,000-person workforce as measured by website analytics.
Rebuilt the interface for ASSURE for Safety, the laboratory’s safety risk model, partnering with a separate data sciences organization and a UX researcher to replace a legacy .NET implementation with 4,714 lines of R in a deployed R Shiny application that showed managers which organizations faced elevated incident risk and which indicators drove it, validated through two rounds of usability testing.
Co-led the 5-person data visualization sub-team supporting a department portfolio of 50+ Tableau and 20+ Shiny visualizations; served as technical lead for the separate 4-person UI/UX data visualization style guide team.
Authored 3 internally used R packages as reusable analytical systems, standardizing database connections, plotting defaults, and package management.
Evaluated Tableau against R Shiny for enterprise visualization delivery, comparing cost, licensing, version control, and customization, and presented the findings to IT staff across the national laboratory system.

Data Analyst, HID Global, Albuquerque, NM, 01/2012–06/2018
As a member of HID Global, a leading provider of secure identity solutions specializing in products and services that enable trusted access to physical and digital spaces. I managed the human testing lab; coordinated 53 research studies, in various sites in the US to evaluate biometric sensors. Analyzed resulting data to measure biometric sensor performance and prepare it for machine learning algorithms. Oversaw 12.89 terabytes of collected data. Presented research findings using various media (print, video, and webinars) to both technical and non-technical staff, and clients. Researched and identified new methods for spoofing biometric devices.

Diagnosed 3 unknown security threats to HID Global biometric sensors that drove improvements to the fake finger detection algorithm; collaborated with hardware engineers and computer scientists on R&D for 4 sensors, including one for guests at the most visited vacation resort in the world.
Programmed a data pipeline processing 3,000 wireless security camera videos collected daily across US research sites for an object detection algorithm.
Cataloged collected data in a MATLAB accessible MySQL database and devised new filename conventions, expediting algorithm development and improving data quality across research sites.
Cut research study cost and product development time by improving subject recruitment, instituting new recruitment methods and strengthening communication to reach a 48% subject retention rate.
Oversaw 12.89 terabytes of collected data across US research sites.

Data Analyst, NMSU Department of Public Health Sciences, Las Cruces, NM, 08/2010–05/2011
Provided statistical consulting to 8 graduate students and 11 faculty members across the full research lifecycle while attending classes full-time: grant writing, hypothesis development, survey and experimental design, data preparation, analysis in SAS and R, and interpretation of results for presentation and publication.

Co-authored a presentation with the university’s associate dean of research applying factor analysis to construct a new metric for measuring hooking-up behavior among college students.
Position created by the department head following demonstrated work in applied statistics, SAS and R programming, and communication with non-technical researchers.

Student Statistical Consultant, NMSU Department of Economics, Applied Statistics, and International Business, Las Cruces, NM, 08/2010–05/2011
Advised graduate students and university staff on statistical methods and software selection, analyzing data in SAS and R across projects on MBA admissions criteria, motel crime rates, and online dating behavior.
Intern Statistician, USDA Food Safety Inspection Service, Washington, DC, 04/2010–08/2010
Ensured data quality for raw data collected across US meat, poultry, and processed egg facilities, cleaning source data and updating the data warehouse. Applied statistical methods to estimate foodborne pathogen prevalence and prepared figures for professional presentations.

Authored a public-facing report on pathogen prevalence in raw poultry products.
Consulted with interns from non-technical backgrounds on appropriate statistical technique for their projects.
